name: Relay
title: Relay
description: Instantly forwards any signal without waiting for dependencies
whenToUse: Forward a signal downstream immediately without waiting on the normal dependency and join rules: a pass-through wire to fan a signal out, or to break a blocking dependency. It adds no transform, only unwrapping a single upstream output and re-timing the signal, so it exists for control-flow rewiring rather than for changing data.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: Signal to relay to downstream nodes

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: flow
package.packageFile:
# FLOW AS MANIFESTS, node by node.
#
# The one package that can migrate INCREMENTALLY, because it declares no credentials. The
# all-or-nothing rule that forced `aws-toolkit` and `cloudinary` to be split came entirely from
# the credential coexistence check (a node needs `credentials/<name>.yaml` in its own package,
# but that file alongside a code `registerCredential` is an error). With no credentials there is
# no conflict, and `src/index.ts` registers each node on its own line — so a node moves by
# writing its manifest and deleting those two lines.
#
# NO allowedHosts, and that is not an omission. Nothing in this package reaches the network at
# all; an empty list means the executor refuses every host, which is exactly right here.
#
# WHAT IS STILL CODE, and why:
#
#   UMAP  runs umap-js IN PROCESS. Genuine local compute, reaching no host. Also of doubtful
#         value as written: it received ONE vector, faked a second by copying it with +0.0001
#         on every element so umap-js would run, and returned near-meaningless coordinates —
#         the real reduction lives in services/umap now. A candidate for removal, undecided.
#
#   SendObject  RETIRED to _legacy, user decision 2026-07-29 — it published to the live
#               session rather than answering the graph, and the `publish` capability that
#               replaced that lane (see Suggestions) covers the need.
#
# Suggestions, which used to sit on this list for the same reason as SendObject, is now a
# manifest: what actually needed code was one push into the caller's template state, and that
# is the executor's `publish` capability (api/publish.yaml) — declared under `requires` below.
#
# AND ONE REMOVAL rather than a migration. Gone from the catalog, so a saved workflow naming
# it now fails to resolve the type:
#
#   MCP             a generic schema-driven mcpService provider from before real service nodes
#                   existed. Superseded by UnoverseMCP in the engine and by per-vendor providers
#                   (HubspotMCP, SalesforceMCP, SlackMCP), so nothing needed it.
#
# FieldValidator was on this list, removed because its five outputs all derive from one
# properties-map cascade and expressions had no way to bind an intermediate value — the cascade
# had to be written out again inside every expression needing it; `completionPercentage` alone
# came to four copies. Named helpers (shared/helpers.yaml) are exactly that binding, so it is
# BACK, same type and connectors, and any workflow that named it resolves again.

name: flow
displayName: Flow
description: Control flow, routing and workflow annotation
version: 2.0.0
category: flow
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

features:
  - Notes and documentation on the canvas
  - Branch, relay and read the running workflow's own context
  - Transform data inline, with optional content ids and run-scoped saved values
  - Loop over an array, running real workflow steps once per item
  - Validate collected data against a schema and get the next missing field to ask for
  - Push suggested FAQs, actions and recommendations to the live chat UI

requires:
  # 1.7.0 for named helpers (shared/helpers.yaml), which FieldValidator's emit rows call —
  # the same floor spatial set when helpers landed. Previously 1.5.0.
  executorVersion: ">=1.7.0"
  # Code's "Save to Context" toggle. Declared even though it cannot silently no-op the way a cache
  # read can — an executor without `save` throws rather than shrugging — because the reason to
  # declare is the same either way: the package says which platform capabilities its nodes need, so
  # installing it against an older executor fails at install rather than at run.
  state:
    - save
  # The LoopStart/LoopEnd pair. More is at stake in declaring these than in most capabilities: an
  # executor that cannot keep an index does not iterate, so an install that skipped this check would
  # run a loop body exactly once and report success.
  loop:
    - open
    - read
    - advance
  # Suggestions' whole job. Declared because on an executor without the publish lane the node
  # would emit its connector and never reach the screen — "worked" everywhere except the one
  # place it matters.
  publish: true

shared.helpers.yaml:
# FLOW'S NAMED FUNCTIONS. FieldValidator's schema cascade and Suggestions' normalizer,
# because both nodes' whole job is shaping one object that several expressions then read.
#
# FieldValidator exists again BECAUSE of this file: it was retired rather than migrated when
# every one of its five outputs derived from the same properties-map cascade and, with no way
# to bind an intermediate value, the cascade had to be written out again inside every
# expression needing it — completionPercentage alone came to four copies. Named helpers are
# the capability that reversed that decision: the cascade runs here, once, and each emit row
# picks one field.
#
# A helper sees only its arguments and its siblings: no config, no credentials, no caller
# scope. Same sandbox as every other expression, no extra authority.

helpers:
  # WHERE THE FIELDS LIVE, across the three shapes the retired node accepted — transcribed
  # from its extractSchemaInfo, cases in the same order:
  #
  #   1. a minted TOOL schema      { inputSchema: { json: { properties, required } } }
  #   2. plain JSON Schema         { properties, required }
  #   3. a bare object             its keys ARE the fields, nothing is required
  #
  # All three still arrive in practice, because the schema is whatever the upstream wire
  # carries: an agent's tool definition, an authored form schema, or a hand-built object.
  schemaInfo:
    args: [schema]
    body: >-
      return (!schema || typeof schema !== 'object')
        ? { fieldNames: [], requiredList: [], propertiesMap: {} }
        : (((schema.inputSchema || {}).json || {}).properties
            ? { fieldNames: Object.keys(schema.inputSchema.json.properties),
                requiredList: schema.inputSchema.json.required || [],
                propertiesMap: schema.inputSchema.json.properties }
            : (schema.properties
                ? { fieldNames: Object.keys(schema.properties),
                    requiredList: schema.required || [],
                    propertiesMap: schema.properties }
                : { fieldNames: Object.keys(schema), requiredList: [], propertiesMap: schema }))

  # A field is MISSING when absent, null, or the empty string — the empty string because these
  # values come off forms and chat slots, where "" is what an unanswered question produces.
  # No data at all means everything is missing, not an error: the first turn of a slot-filling
  # conversation legitimately starts from nothing.
  missingFields:
    args: [fieldNames, data]
    body: >-
      return (!data || typeof data !== 'object')
        ? fieldNames
        : fieldNames.filter(f => data[f] == null || data[f] === '')

  # THE SUGGESTIONS OBJECT, normalized at the source — transcribed from the retired
  # Suggestions executor. The template's contract is `{ text }` (the SDK stores producer data
  # opaquely and knows no "faq", UNOVERSE_STATE_MODEL §8), while authors write a string,
  # `{ text }` or `{ question }` — so the flattening happens HERE and the SDK never has to.
  #
  # Per-key fallback, signal over config, exactly as the retired node resolved it: a workflow
  # usually wires the whole object off an upstream extractor, and static config is the
  # standing default for whichever keys the signal does not carry.
  #
  # The retired node's two-level "source node / output handle" probing is deliberately NOT
  # transcribed: that unwrapped the LEGACY engine's signal envelope, and the manifest executor
  # binds the payload by input port name instead — there is nothing left to unwrap.
  suggestionsOf:
    args: [given, authored]
    body: >-
      return ((sig) => ({
        faqs: ((sig.faqs || authored.faqs) || []).map(f => ({
          text: typeof f === 'string'
            ? f
            : ((f || {}).text != null ? f.text : ((f || {}).question != null ? f.question : ''))
        })),
        actions: (sig.actions || authored.actions) || [],
        recommendations: (sig.recommendations || authored.recommendations) || []
      }))(given || {})

  # ONE report with everything the node emits. `null` rather than `undefined` for an absent
  # next field, so the emit rows can test it with a plain comparison.
  #
  # NEXT-FIELD PRIORITY is the retired node's: first missing field that the schema marks
  # required, else first missing field in schema order — `filter(...)[0] || missing[0]`
  # collapses both cases because an empty filter yields undefined and falls through.
  fieldReport:
    args: [schema, data]
    body: >-
      return ((info) =>
        ((missing) =>
          ((next) => ({
            nextField: next,
            nextFieldSchema: (next == null || info.propertiesMap[next] == null)
              ? null
              : info.propertiesMap[next],
            missingFields: missing,
            isComplete: missing.length === 0,
            completionPercentage: info.fieldNames.length === 0
              ? 100
              : Math.round((info.fieldNames.length - missing.length) / info.fieldNames.length * 100)
          }))(missing.length === 0
            ? null
            : (missing.filter(f => info.requiredList.includes(f))[0] || missing[0]))
        )(helpers.missingFields(info.fieldNames, data))
      )(helpers.schemaInfo(schema))

files.api/events.yaml:
# NO CALLS. This node reaches no host: it forwards a signal, and `events` is the whole of it.
#
# THE UNWRAP, transcribed from the retired executor rather than reinvented. An incoming signal is
# nested twice — by INPUT PORT, then by SOURCE NODE ID, then by that source's OUTPUT HANDLE:
#
#     { signal: { upstream1: { output: { message: "relay me" } } } }
#
# The retired node peeled that down to the innermost payload so a downstream node received the DATA
# rather than the envelope, and the three branches below are its three branches:
#
#   one source, ONE output handle    forward the inner payload            { message: "relay me" }
#   one source, SEVERAL handles      forward the source's whole object    { a: …, b: … }
#   no `signal` port at all          forward the inputs untouched
#
# Peeling only a single handle is deliberate: with two handles there is no single payload to choose,
# so keeping the object is the only answer that loses nothing.

- emit: signal
  value: >-
    return !response.signal
      ? response
      : (Object.keys(response.signal).length === 0
          ? {}
          : (Object.keys(Object.values(response.signal)[0] || {}).length === 1
              ? Object.values(Object.values(response.signal)[0])[0]
              : Object.values(response.signal)[0]))

files.node.yaml:
type: Relay
kind: PromiseNode

name: Relay
category: Flow
color: "#10B981"

description: Instantly forwards any signal without waiting for dependencies

whenToUse: >-
  Forward a signal downstream immediately without waiting on the normal dependency and join rules: a
  pass-through wire to fan a signal out, or to break a blocking dependency. It adds no transform,
  only unwrapping a single upstream output and re-timing the signal, so it exists for control-flow
  rewiring rather than for changing data.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NOT cacheable: it forwards whatever arrived, and what arrives differs every run.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
# The retired node's own fixture, unchanged, because it documents the nesting: the payload arrives
# under the input PORT, then the SOURCE NODE, then that source's OUTPUT HANDLE.
#
# Asserting `message` at the TOP of the output is the whole point — it proves the envelope was peeled
# off. A relay that forwarded `{ upstream1: { output: … } }` would look like it worked while handing
# every downstream node the wrapper instead of the data.

testData:
  config: {}
  inputs:
    signal:
      upstream1:
        output:
          message: relay me
  expect:
    signal: "return output.signal.message === 'relay me'"
